content: Cluster-adjusted analyses were incorporated into the meta-analysis for cluster-randomized trials. Two individual randomized trials and two cluster-randomized trials were included. We downgraded the evidence once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) in all trials and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in two trials. The original sample size did not represent the effective cluster-adjusted sample size in the meta-analysis. In the meta-analysis, Choko (2019a) had multiple intervention arms involving HIV self-testing (HIVST) with similar kit distribution methods, so all intervention arms were combined. Choko (2019b) had two intervention arms with HIVST and two subgroups (antenatal care [ANC] women and antiretroviral therapy [ART] clients); only the ANC group was included in this analysis. Cluster-adjusted analyses were included for cluster-randomized trials. One individual randomized trial and two cluster-randomized trials were included. We downgraded the evidence once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) in all trials and unclear risk of attrition bias in one trial. Two cluster-randomized trials were subject to recruitment bias, and one trial had an unclear risk of cluster loss and did not report cluster-adjusted analyses (adjusted for clustering in the meta-analysis). The meta-analysis included Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017), which had more than one intervention arm involving HIVST but with different kit distribution methods. Only the HIVST arm with direct distribution to peers was included, and the control arm sample was adjusted to prevent double counting. Cluster-adjusted analyses were included for cluster-randomized trials. Two cluster-randomized trials were included. We downgraded the evidence once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in both trials. The original sample size did not represent the effective cluster-adjusted sample size in the meta-analysis. Three individual randomized trials and six cluster-randomized trials were included. We downgraded the evidence once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) in eight trials, detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in three trials, and attrition bias in one trial. Two cluster-randomized trials were subject to recruitment bias, and one trial experienced cluster loss. Some risk of bias domains was unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. The measurement time points varied (range: 2 weeks to 5 months), and point estimates from individual studies also varied (25% to 76%). We downgraded the evidence once. The meta-analysis included Choko (2019a), which had multiple intervention arms involving HIVST with different linkage interventions. Arms with similar linkage interventions were combined. Choko (2019b) had two intervention arms with HIVST and different linkage interventions; arms were not combined. Shahmanesh (2019) had two different interventions, and arms were not combined. Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017) had more than one intervention arm involving HIVST with different kit distribution methods but no linkage intervention; arms were combined, and the control arm sample was adjusted to prevent double counting. Cluster-adjusted analyses were included for cluster-randomized trials. Five individual randomized trials and seven cluster-randomized trials were included. We downgraded the evidence once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) in all trials, detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in five trials, unclear risk of detection bias in one trial, and unclear attrition bias in one trial. Three cluster-randomized trials were subject to recruitment bias. Several risk of bias domains were unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. Subgroup analysis showed that heterogeneity was explained by population type. Outcome definitions were inconsistent across trials: seven trials defined linkage as ART initiation, whereas five defined it as linkage to any HIV care. Two trials were conducted among female sex workers, and subgroup analysis among women was included for two trials. The meta-analysis included Chanda (2017) and Ortblad (2017), which had more than one intervention arm involving HIVST but with different kit distribution methods. Intervention arms were not combined, and the control arm sample was adjusted to prevent double counting. Cluster-adjusted analyses were included for cluster-randomized trials. One individual randomized trial and two cluster-randomized trials were included. We downgraded the evidence once due to potential performance bias (lack of blinding) in all trials and detection bias (self-reported or non-validated outcomes) in two trials. Two trials had unclear risk of selection bias (one random sequence generation, two allocation concealment), and some risk of bias domains were unclear due to insufficient information from unpublished reports or conference abstracts. For both trials, subgroup analysis among young people was included.
